name: Carla Molina
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember the porch with the permanently crooked curtain.” On Monday, near the entrance to the Wash House, Carla stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: I am the postal substitute. I know the houses by curtains until everybody changes them.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a cropped bottle-green coat and a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. Carla has a narrow face with an expressive upper lip, with dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. Carla takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Carla is fond of ambitious ideas and deeply suspicious of grand openings. The question Carla asks at any launch is who has the keys for cleaning up a month later.
agenda: To draw a route that works after the curtains change.
family: Faye Boone is Carla’s cousin. Carla makes the call. Faye is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *Reopening at six*, Faye says, “I live over the machines. I want one night when I can hear my husband's voice in bed.”
connections: Darcy Bay. A substitute carrier draws the porch on a card for the pensioner driver.

reactions.situation: A delivery goes to the newly renumbered neighbor
reactions.response: Carla checks both doorways before moving the delivery.
